meanings.note: Having no interest or concern. Privative prefix 'без-' ('without, -less') (stem 'различный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('indifferent, uncaring').

examples.trans: Nothing of the sort, you mean nothing to me!

examples.text: Я докажу, что она мне безразлична.
examples.trans: I will prove that she means nothing to me.

meanings.note: the present tense is normally left out: я мэр = I am the mayor
Present есть; у меня есть = I have. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to be; there is'.
future: буду / будешь ... + infinitive

examples.trans: You will be asking for forgiveness.

meanings.note: + prepositional (where). Core Russian prep meaning 'in, into' in everyday speech.
+ accusative (where to). Core Russian prep meaning 'in, into' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: The neuter form 'всё' used alone. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.
Neuter всё. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.
Plural все. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.
Core Russian adv meaning 'yesterday' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Я вчера ел маринованные грибы. Может, один гриб был плохой.
examples.trans: Yesterday I ate pickled mushrooms. Maybe one mushroom was bad.

meanings.note: polite to one person, or to several people

meanings.en: other forms: вас (gen/acc), вам (dat), вами (instr), вас (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'you (polite or plural)' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Also 'girlfriend' (моя девушка). Common feminine noun meaning 'young woman; girlfriend' in everyday Russian.
Своя девушка. Common feminine noun meaning 'young woman; girlfriend' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: У мужчины, мальчик, бывает не только жена. Это моя девушка.
examples.trans: A man, my boy, can have more than just a wife. She's my girlfriend.

meanings.note: на днях = in the next few days, or the other day

examples.trans: I'll call in the next few days.
Any day now, on the website.

meanings.note: + genitive. Core Russian prep meaning 'for' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: We could open a salon for you.

examples.text: Для вас можно открыть салон красоты.
examples.trans: We could open a beauty salon for you.

meanings.note: что и требовалось доказать = Q.E.D., which is what needed to be proved

examples.trans: There, which is what needed to be proved!

examples.text: Я обязательно докажу своё кулинарное мастерство.
examples.trans: I will definitely prove my culinary mastery.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'friendship' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Конечно, между нами только крепкая искренняя дружба.
examples.trans: Of course, between us there is only strong sincere friendship.

meanings.note: Спасибо за + accusative. Core Russian prep meaning 'for; behind' in everyday speech.
+ instrumental. Core Russian prep meaning 'for; behind' in everyday speech.
Verbal action/result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание'. Common neuter noun meaning 'meaning, significance' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Для меня это не имеет значения.
examples.trans: For me that does not matter.

meanings.note: emphasis: вот поэтому ты и... = that's exactly why you...

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Core Russian conj meaning 'or' in everyday speech.
mostly in set phrases: иметь совесть, иметь право = to have the right; everyday 'I have' is у меня есть

examples.trans: You have the right to remain silent.

examples.text: Нина, имей совесть! Я вчера ради вас всё сделал.
examples.trans: Nina, have a heart! Yesterday I did everything for you.

meanings.note: Question word. Core Russian adv meaning 'how; as' in everyday speech.
Как вы знаете = as you know. Core Russian adv meaning 'how; as' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.en: by the way, speaking of which
meanings.note: Used as a parenthetical word. Core Russian adv meaning 'by the way; handy' in everyday speech.
Это очень кстати. Core Russian adv meaning 'by the way; handy' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Oh, by the way, I almost forgot.

examples.text: Кстати, если хочешь, иди к нам в команду. Шансы у нас огромные.
examples.trans: By the way, if you want, join our team. Our chances are huge.

meanings.note: + instrumental; между собой = between yourselves/themselves

examples.trans: You two sort it out between yourselves here.
There are no secrets between us.

examples.text: Ну ладно, вы тут между собой договоритесь.
examples.trans: All right, you two sort it out between yourselves here.

meanings.note: Agrees with the thing owned. Core Russian det meaning 'my, mine' in everyday speech.
наш, наша, наше, наши; agrees with the noun

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates
Negative prefix 'не-' ('un-, non-, not') (stem 'доразумение'). Verbal action/result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание'. Common neuter noun meaning 'misunderstanding' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: There was a terrible misunderstanding this morning.

examples.text: Утром вышло страшное недоразумение. Я не сразу вас узнал.
examples.trans: There was a terrible misunderstanding this morning. I didn't recognise you right away.

meanings.note: + genitive: 'у нас нет выбора' = we have no choice
+ genitive. Core Russian part meaning 'no; there isn't' in everyday speech.
usually in the genitive ничего, with не: ничего не осталось

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: Locative на носу. Common masculine noun meaning 'nose' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Когда не можешь сам себе нос вытереть.
examples.trans: When you can't even wipe your own nose yourself.

examples.text: От холода у него покраснел нос.
examples.trans: His nose turned red from the cold.

examples.text: У меня скоро долгожданная пенсия на носу.
examples.trans: My long-awaited pension is right around the corner.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'to her', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Она нашла нас на новом месте.
examples.trans: She found us at the new place.
That is it, she got really offended.
She is not answering her phone.

meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'валить'). Used in Russian as a perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to back off'.

examples.text: Отвали, или я сломаю тебе нос!
examples.trans: Back off, or I will break your nose!

meanings.note: Informal. Core Russian interj meaning 'bye' in everyday speech.
As an adverb. Core Russian interj meaning 'bye' in everyday speech.

meanings.en: to have a look, to take a look
meanings.note: One completed look. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'смотреть'). Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to have a look', paired with 'смотреть'.
Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'смотреть'). Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to have a look', paired with 'смотреть'.

examples.trans: Can I go and have a look?

meanings.note: Asks about the reason.

examples.trans: Why are we going so slowly?

examples.text: Виталик, почему мы так медленно едем? Быстрее!
examples.trans: Vitalik, why are we going so slowly? Faster!

meanings.note: Single act of betrayal. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to betray'.

examples.trans: I will not betray my native land.
I will not betray my native land!

examples.text: Твой дед в войну родину предал.
examples.trans: Your grandfather betrayed his country in the war.

meanings.note: Informal: family and friends. Core Russian interj meaning 'hi' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: Прямо так = just like that. Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.
Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: В смысле, Виктор Степанович? Прямо так, да?
examples.trans: What do you mean, Viktor Stepanovich? Just like that?

meanings.note: Dining establishment. Borrowed from French 'restaurant' (from 'restaurer', to restore strength with rich broth); entered Russian in the early 19th century.

examples.trans: They called from the Italian restaurant.
In the evening they went to a restaurant.

examples.text: Кстати, звонили из итальянского ресторана. Дарят папе романтический ужин на двоих.
examples.trans: By the way, they called from the Italian restaurant. They're giving Dad a romantic dinner for two.

meanings.note: + instrumental; со before some consonant clusters: со всеми

examples.trans: Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'делать'). Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to do, to make', paired with 'делать'.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need to do even more.

meanings.en: to be angry, to be cross
meanings.note: На + accusative = at someone. Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to be angry', paired with 'рассердиться'.

examples.text: Нин, только не сердись, ладно? Он всё помоет.
examples.trans: Nina, just don't be angry, okay? He'll wash everything.

meanings.note: Сломать руку = to break one's arm. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ломать'). Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to break', paired with 'ломать'.

examples.text: Меня жена бросила. Два пальца сломаны.
examples.trans: My wife has left me. Two of my fingers are broken.

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('accidental').

examples.trans: It was a completely accidental misunderstanding.

examples.text: Ты абсолютно прав, мой случайный собеседник.
examples.trans: You are absolutely right, my chance interlocutor.

meanings.note: Совершенно верно = quite right. Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Совершенно верно, я мэр этого города.
examples.trans: Quite right, I am the mayor of this town.
This is a completely new car.

examples.text: Совершенно верно, я мэр этого города. И предложение у меня к вам такое.
examples.trans: Quite right, I am the mayor of this town. And my offer to you is this.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to sleep', paired with 'поспать'.

examples.text: Ладно, утром позвоню ей. Поехали спать.
examples.trans: All right, I'll call her in the morning. Let's go to sleep.

meanings.note: To someone you call ты. Core Russian det meaning 'your (informal)' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Я бы на твоём месте подумал.
examples.trans: If I were you, I'd think about it.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'technically'.

examples.text: Кстати, технически она пока не твоя.
examples.trans: By the way, technically she is not yours yet.

meanings.note: One person, informal. Core Russian pron meaning 'you (informal)' in everyday speech.

meanings.en: other forms: тебя (gen/acc), тебе (dat), тобой (instr), тебе (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'you (informal)' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: + infinitive or a noun. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to want', paired with 'захотеть'.

examples.trans: If you don't want to, suit yourself.
They want to build a shopping centre there.

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to kiss'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense. The reflexive suffix '-ся'/'-сь' makes the action intransitive, reciprocal, or directed at the subject.

examples.trans: They were kissing for a long time.

examples.text: Ты вчера целовался с моей девушкой!

examples.trans: You were kissing right in the restaurant!

meanings.note: Question word. Core Russian pron meaning 'what' in everyday speech.
Conjunction. Core Russian pron meaning 'what' in everyday speech.
Core Russian pron meaning 'what' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: pointing at a thing or a situation; 'это' + noun = 'this is ...'
points at something: это моё = that's mine
Linking word: главное — это народ. Core Russian pron meaning 'this, that; it is' in everyday speech.

meanings.en: other forms: этого, этому, это, этим, этом
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'this, that; it is' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.note: меня = me (genitive/accusative), мне = to me (dative)

meanings.en: other forms: меня (gen/acc), мне (dat), мной (instr), мне (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'I' in everyday speech.
